question: Does @nx/angular@23.1.1 route through the deprecated @angular-devkit/build-angular on Angular 22, or through @angular/build?
gates: ADR-012 (open item) — additionally measures two ADR-004 assumptions
method: A real Nx 23.1.1 workspace was created, a publishable Angular library and an application were generated, @angular-devkit/build-angular was physically removed from node_modules, and both builds were run. Source reading was used only to locate what to test; every verdict below comes from an executed build.
packageManagerScope: npm. ADR-012 mandates pnpm. Executor routing is package-manager-independent; the transitive-install observation in Q2 is npm-specific and MUST be re-measured under pnpm during Phase 1.

Q1_executorRouting.question: Do the executors TEKAD would use call @angular-devkit/build-angular?

applicationExecutor.observed: @nx/angular:application asserts @angular/build is installed and imports buildApplication from it

libraryExecutor.observed: calls ngPackagr() from ng-packagr directly, with an Nx stylesheet-processor provider; the only @angular-devkit/build-angular reference on this path is a type-only import in schema.d.ts

decisiveTest.action: moved node_modules/@angular-devkit/build-angular out of the tree, then ran both builds

Q1_executorRouting.verdict: @nx/angular 23.1.1 does NOT route through @angular-devkit/build-angular for the application or library build paths on Angular 22. OBSERVED.

Q2_isItStillInstalled.question: Even if unused, does it end up in the dependency tree?

observed.angularMonorepoPresetDeclaresIt: yes — @angular-devkit/build-angular@22.0.6 appears in `dependencies` of the scaffolded package.json
observed.npmDeprecationWarningEmitted: npm warn deprecated @angular-devkit/build-angular@22.0.6: Angular's Webpack support is deprecated. Use the esbuild and Vite-based "@angular/build" package instead.
observed.afterRemovingTheDirectDependency: still resolvable in node_modules under npm; it is an OPTIONAL peer of both @nx/angular and @analogjs/vite-plugin-angular (the vitest-analog runner the preset chose)

Q2_isItStillInstalled.verdict: It is DECLARED by the preset template and pulled as an optional peer under npm, but it is NOT on any build path TEKAD uses. Declaration is a hygiene problem, not a correctness one.

Q3_tsSolutionSetup.question: Does Nx 23's default TypeScript setup work with @nx/angular generators?

observed.nx23DefaultWorkspace: tsconfig.base.json with composite:true + emitDeclarationOnly + customConditions, root tsconfig.json with `references: []`, package.json `workspaces: ["packages/*"]`
observed.generatorResult: REFUSED — "The \"@nx/angular:library\" generator doesn't support the existing TypeScript setup. The Angular framework doesn't support a TypeScript setup with project references. See https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/37276"
observed.escapeHatch: NX_IGNORE_UNSUPPORTED_TS_SETUP=true — explicitly documented by Nx as "at your own risk"
observed.angularTemplateSetup: the angular-monorepo template instead emits a legacy tsconfig.base.json with `paths`, no composite, no npm workspaces

Q3_tsSolutionSetup.verdict: TEKAD must scaffold with the legacy path-mapping TypeScript setup, not Nx 23's default TS-solution setup. OBSERVED. This is a Phase 1 constraint that was not previously recorded.

Q4_presetFidelity.question: Is `create-nx-workspace --preset=angular-monorepo` usable as TEKAD's scaffold?
Q4_presetFidelity.observed: the preset now resolves to a fixed GitHub template (nrwl/angular-template) and IGNORED --appName, --ssr and --routing; it scaffolded a fixed shop/api e-commerce demo with SSR, Express, Playwright, Docker and vitest-analog
Q4_presetFidelity.verdict: NOT usable as TEKAD's scaffold. Phase 1 must build the workspace from an empty base and add Angular projects with generators, not from this preset.

Q5_angularVersionPin.question: Which Angular version does @nx/angular 23.1.1 scaffold?
Q5_angularVersionPin.implication: The generator will not reach Angular 22.1.x, which is the version the P0/P1 research targeted. Phase 1 must pin Angular explicitly after scaffolding rather than accepting the generator's range.
Q5_angularVersionPin.verdict: OBSERVED — a version-pin step is required in Phase 1.

Q6_twoLevelEntryPoints.question: Does @nx/angular:package support ADR-004's two-level, category-prefixed entry points?

observed.generatorOutput: @nx/angular:library-secondary-entry-point creates a FLAT one-level entry point and scaffolds an NgModule, which does not match TEKAD's standalone-only, two-level topology
observed.handAuthoredTwoLevel: libs/probelib/components/input/ with its own ng-package.json was auto-discovered and built without any registration
observed.wildcardSubpath: none emitted — ./src/* is unimportable by default

Q6_twoLevelEntryPoints.verdict: SUPPORTED. OBSERVED. The emitted exports map is exactly the shape Spike A proved tsserver resolves for auto-import, so Spike A and Spike B chain into an end-to-end result.

Q7_crossEntryPointImports.question: What happens when one entry point imports another?

relativeImportAcrossBoundary.message: Cannot destructure property 'pos' of 'file.referencedFiles[index]' as it is undefined.
relativeImportAcrossBoundary.note: The failure is correct but the diagnostic is an internal crash, not a readable 'not part of any entry point' error. This is a contributor-DX hazard and argues for a lint rule that catches it before ng-packagr does.

packageNameImportAcrossBoundary.observedEmission: import { sharedHelper } from '@tekad-probe/probelib' is left UNRESOLVED in each secondary FESM; the shared code exists once, in the primary FESM

Q7_crossEntryPointImports.verdict: ng-packagr emits no shared CHUNK files, but it also does not duplicate: it defers deduplication to the consumer's bundler by emitting bare package-name imports. The practical outcome is no duplication. OBSERVED.

Q8_treeShaking.question: Does importing one secondary entry point drag the whole primary entry point into a consumer bundle?
Q8_treeShaking.method: The BUILT package was installed into node_modules (not consumed from source); an app imported only @tekad-probe/probelib/components/input; a distinctive ballast symbol exported from the primary entry point and used by nothing was searched for in the production browser bundle.

positiveControl.action: the app was rebuilt with an explicit import of the ballast symbol

Q8_treeShaking.verdict: Unused primary-entry-point code IS tree-shaken out of a consumer bundle that imports only a secondary entry point. OBSERVED, with a passing positive control.

outstanding: Re-measure Q2 under pnpm — a non-flat node_modules changes how an optional peer resolves.

Q8 measured ONE ballast symbol in ONE app. ADR-004's standing requirement for a CI tree-shaking probe app is NOT discharged by this spike; it is now known to be achievable, not known to hold for the real package graph.
The @nx/angular:library-secondary-entry-point generator emits an NgModule and a flat path. TEKAD needs its own generator or a documented manual convention.
